index_inputs.title: Evaluation protocol
index_inputs.body: > Status: **draft / scaffold**. The full protocol will codify the rules used inside ScienceVision for whitelist and judge defenses. BabyVision-v2 follows the BabyVision v1 methodology: **executable ground truth first, LLM judge only as a tiebreaker.** 1. **Numeric / geometric truth** (preferred): distances, angles, topology counts, volumes, interference flags. Exact match or epsilon-tolerance. 2. **Pixel truth**: SSIM and LPIPS thresholds for rendered/segmented outputs. 3. **Structured-answer truth**: format with strict parsing. 4. **LLM judge** (last resort): only invoked when the above three are inapplicable. Always logged for audit. For and , the is parsed and replayed against the MCP server to verify the agent's claimed tool calls are real and consistent with its final answer. Every submission must include enough metadata for a third party to replay: - Model version / commit - Sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, seed) - Compute environment (GPU, OS) for renderers - Pinned dependency versions

index_inputs.title: Positioning — measuring the impact of 3D vision on reasoning
index_inputs.body: > Where BabyVision-v2 sits relative to other visual-reasoning benchmarks, and > what it adds. Most multimodal reasoning benchmarks bundle two questions together: *does the model reason well?* and *is vision actually being used?* When a benchmark only reports an aggregate accuracy, a high score can come from text shortcuts, language priors over image captions, or memorized solutions — none of which require the model to look at the image at all. The benchmarks below were chosen because they each address some part of **"how do we measure the contribution of vision (especially 3D vision) to reasoning?"** They cluster into three groups plus the direct predecessor: 1. **Static 2D visual necessity** — control for text-only shortcuts on static images. 2. **3D scene understanding** — input is real or simulated 3D geometry, not just images of it. 3. **Embodied / interactive 3D** — vision must drive grounding, navigation, or manipulation, not just answer questions. 4. **BabyVision v1** — same lab; the predecessor that established the executable-GT / no-LLM-judge methodology on 2D visual reasoning, which v2 inherits and extends. BabyVision-v2 sits across (2) and (3) with one extra commitment the others do not make: **executable ground truth** (geometry, mask argmax, physics solver output), so the score is defended without an LLM-as-judge. | Benchmark | Year | Visual input | How vision is tested | Ground truth | Agent / tool use | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | MMMU-Pro | 2024 | 2D images, multi-discipline | Filters text-only-answerable items; adds vision-only (screenshot) setting | Multiple choice | — | | BLINK | 2024 | 2D images / image pairs | Perception primitives (depth, correspondence, multi-view) that language can't mediate | Multiple choice | — | | MathVerse | 2024 | 2D math figures | Per-question variants moving information between text and figure | Pattern-match against canonical answer | — | | SciVerse | 2025 | 2D scientific figures | Knowledge × vision × CoT ablation (knowledge-free/lite/rich × vision-rich/vision-only) | Pattern-match against canonical answer | — | | EmbodiedBench | 2025 | Multi-view, simulated 3D | Vision-driven embodied multi-task: navigation, manipulation, planning, spatial awareness | Task success rate | ✓ (action) | | Embodied3DBench | 2026 | 3D scenes, multi-view | Directly tests VLM 3D priors: grounding, spatial relation, multi-view correspondence, affordance, grasp, trajectory | Spatial labels / coordinates | partial | | EPIC-Bench | 2026 | Real embodied images | Anti-MCQ-shortcut: fine-grained visual grounding required for target localization → navigation → manipulation | Localization + nav + manip outcomes | ✓ (action) | | BabyVision v1 | 2026 | 2D images | Child-level visual primitives that defeat language priors (reported Gemini3-Pro-Preview 49.7% vs Human 94.1%) | Executable / structured — the anti-LLM-judge methodology v2 inherits | — | | **BabyVision-v2** | **2026** | **3D scenes + interactive physics + viewer** | **Profile separation: every submission tagged / / , so the contribution of vision is isolable in the leaderboard** | **Executable: numeric (distance, angle, topology, volume) + pixel (SSIM/LPIPS) + structured ; LLM judge only as last-resort tiebreaker** | **✓ (MCP tools, trace replayed against server)** | The row above BV2 is the direct predecessor: v1 established the executable-GT / no-LLM-judge methodology on 2D visual reasoning. v2 keeps that methodology and extends along three axes — real 3D scene grounding, professional domains, and agent operation traces with pixel evidence (see ). (Years and source links for the 2026 embodied entries are recorded in ; they may be preprints at the time of writing.) The same eight benchmarks, scored against the capabilities that matter for measuring vision's contribution to reasoning. Rows 1–2 are strengths inherited from 2D visual-necessity work (MMMU-Pro / BLINK / MathVerse / SciVerse); rows 3–4 are inherited from embodied / 3D work (EmbodiedBench / Embodied3DBench / EPIC-Bench); rows 5–8 are the gaps BV2 closes that none of the predecessors close together. The text-shortcut filtering culture comes from MMMU-Pro; perception-primitive testing from BLINK; 3D-geometry input from the embodied cluster; agent traces from EPIC-Bench / EmbodiedBench. - Rows 5–8 are where no single prior benchmark covers what BV2 covers together: a *layered* evaluation stack (geometric + pixel + structured, with LLM judge only as a tiebreaker), tool-trace replay for fidelity, and per-submission profile separation that turns "is vision doing work?" into a leaderboard-level question rather than an ablation paper. - The BV1 column documents the inherited methodology: same anti-LLM-judge posture and structured-answer parsing on 2D primitives. v2 keeps that spine and adds the rows that depend on a real 3D scene + a tool surface. See for the layered defense in detail and for the profile spec. - **Not a meta-leaderboard.** We do not re-run other benchmarks; numbers from the works above belong on their own leaderboards. - **Not a comprehensive survey.** The four sources under catalogue ~30 additional benchmarks (HallusionBench, MMVP, VisuLogic, CHAIN, EgoBench, OpenEQA, …) — the seven shown here were picked as the most informative representatives of each cluster for the question *"is vision doing real work?"*. The full sets are worth reading when designing a new task family. - **Not a comparison with VLA-model diagnostic work.** Papers like FocusVLA, VLA-Trace, VLM4VLA, and CoT-VLA diagnose **models**, not benchmarks, so they belong in a separate discussion (see ).

With Stages 1–3 split apart, we evaluate the orthogonal question: "does a *general* VLM, when paired with the right segmentation tool, recover the gap to a joint-trained model?" index_inputs.body: Status: **v3 — filtered to 3D-vision-load-bearing tasks** (2026-06-05) Scope: design contract for the K-axis seed family in the ScienceVision QA-gen pipeline. History: v1 design (PR #78) → v2 seed-fill realization (PR #81) → v3 filter + reframing (this revision). > **Reading order:** start with > for the stage / template / cell-iteration vocabulary; this file is the > worked design for one specific seed family on top of that base. --- The **K-axis** (knowledge-grounded spatial relations) covers a specific class of CT QA tasks: ones that require **both** professional medical knowledge **and** active 3D vision in the viewer, where neither alone is sufficient. Concretely, a task qualifies as K-axis if and only if **both** of these are necessary to produce the answer: - **(a) Professional medical knowledge** — anatomy naming, pathology mapping, staging frameworks, normal-variant ranges. This is what a trained radiologist brings. - **(b) Active 3D viewer interaction** — slice navigation, window-leveled CT intensity reading at the mask boundary, pairwise mask-anatomy spatial reasoning under partial-volume averaging, multi-axis confirmation of (non-)invasion. This is what *cannot* be recovered from a single rendered thumbnail or from paraphrase. If either component alone is sufficient, the task does not belong on the K-axis. - **Not** "open-ended medical VQA". K-axis tasks have enumerated answer schemas; the candidate sets are case-specific and finite. - **Not** pure visual classification. The candidate labels carry clinical meaning the model must *interpret*, not just match against pixel patterns. - **Not** the existing V1–V6 axis in . V-axis tests viewing-skill primitives (slice planning, visibility, annotation, consistency, trace, topology). K-axis tests viewing-skill **fused with** domain knowledge. The V and K axes can in principle be combined cell-wise (e.g. V3-K3 = "annotate the mask component that supports the topology answer"), but the seeds in this document are pure-K — they specify what K alone means. The first attempt at this design (v1, PR #79) proposed K1–K5 — five templates covering containment, wall-vs-lumen, multi-mask relation, DDx ranking, and negative-containment. v2 filled the template slots per case. Reviewing v2 in the viewer made one issue obvious: not all five templates **needed the viewer** to be answered. - **K1 (containment + diagnosis from a 6-option list)** — once the prompt names the anatomy ("aortic wall") and lists the six candidates, a medically-knowledgeable model can pick the answer from the mask_text description alone. Opening the volume does not change the most-likely answer. - **K4 (DDx ranking of 4 supplied candidates)** — the ranking depends on demographics + finding description, not on whether the model navigated through axial slices. v3 drops K1 and K4 for not passing criterion (b). The retained templates — K2, K3, K5 — are the ones where 3D viewing is *answer-determining*. Anchored on M3D-RefSeg cases present on disk and on the strict-whitelist Tier-1 list. **Question shape.** *Given a high-density focus mask inside a named vessel/organ, decide whether it sits in the wall, the lumen, or surrounding tissue, and state the pathology that sub-location implies.* **Why 3D viewing is load-bearing.** The same mask shape can come from wall calcification (atherosclerosis) or intraluminal embolus (thrombus). To distinguish, the model must window-level the CT intensity *at the mask boundary*: a wall finding sits at the density-transition between vessel lumen (~50 HU enhanced) and surrounding tissue (~30 HU), and the mask edge aligns with the high-density rim, not the lumen interior. **Answer schema.** **Pilot binding.** (aortic-wall calcification → atherosclerosis), seed answer . **Question shape.** *Given a labeled mask component A and a named anatomy B, classify the spatial relation A↔B as one of {contains, contained_by, adjacent, disjoint}, and state whether that relation is pathologically significant.* **Why 3D viewing is load-bearing.** Partial-volume averaging at the mask edge makes "contains" vs "adjacent" not separable from boolean overlap of voxel sets. The model must visually judge whether the two components share a continuous interface (adjacent), one envelops the other (contains/contained_by), or they sit at different anatomic levels (disjoint). The K3 forbidden-tool list explicitly bans and to enforce this. **Answer schema.** **Pilot binding.** (peritoneal nodule × sigmoid colon wall), seed answer (peritoneal carcinomatosis = M1c). **Question shape.** *Given a masked lesion and a named adjacent structure, determine whether the lesion crosses into that structure, and map the answer to a clinical label under a stated framework (tumor staging, infection extension).* **Why 3D viewing is load-bearing.** A correct **NEGATIVE** answer (no invasion) is only justified if absence-of-breach can be confirmed on at least two orthogonal slices. A single-slice projection can hide oblique invasion. K5 enforces to make orthogonal-view confirmation a scoring gate. **Answer schema.** **Pilot bindings.** - (peritoneal nodule × sigmoid colon wall, AJCC TNM peritoneal-metastasis frame), seed answer . - (inguinal high-density shadow × femoral neurovascular bundle, soft-tissue infection extension frame), seed answer . Its command must remain distinct from the root project's command. Authoring and evaluation data cross the boundary in separate artifacts: - The solver receives only the prompt, an anonymous scene reference, and a constrained viewer-session request. It must not receive a source asset ID or path, reference answer, seed, internal knowledge, credential, or audit data. - The scorer receives the answer and rubric material needed to evaluate the solver output. Scorer artifacts are never solver-visible. - Real asset resolution, evidence, reviews, receipts, and audit artifacts stay on the trusted host side. Anonymous scene references are resolved there, not in the solver bundle. The package's leakage check is the release gate for solver-visible artifacts. Mirroring source code and static fixtures does not publish any runtime bundle. BabyVision keeps its existing Mol* and NiiVue pages as the renderer owners. The vNext mirror adds the source-pinned contract and the two family-specific adapters as in-page, schema-validated bridges. They register only after their viewer has loaded and fail closed when loading fails; they do not create a network API or give a solver access to source files. The bridge is capability evidence, not a release exception. A vNext medical solver session still receives an anonymous scene reference only, and the package's controlled viewer/release checks must keep masks and overlays outside the solver-visible bundle. exposes only session-local structure identifiers, indexes, visibility, and element counts.
